bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

### Emacs

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

### TextMate

TextMate users can use Ag with [my fork](https://github.com/ggreer/AckMate) of the popular AckMate plugin, which lets you use both Ack and Ag for searching. If you already have AckMate you just want to replace Ack with Ag, move or delete `"~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"` and run `ln -s /usr/local/bin/ag "~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"`

## Other stuff you might like

* [Ack](https://github.com/petdance/ack3) - Better than grep. Without Ack, Ag would not exist.
* [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim)
* [Exuberant Ctags](http://ctags.sourceforge.net/) - Faster than Ag, but it builds an index beforehand. Good for *really* big codebases.
* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

## Documentation

For detailed usage information and command-line options, see the manual page in the `doc/` directory.
</output>

     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

ag(1) -- The Silver Searcher. Like ack, but faster.
=============================================

## SYNOPSIS

`ag` [_options_] _pattern_ [_path ..._]

## DESCRIPTION

Recursively search for PATTERN in PATH. Like grep or ack, but faster.

## OPTIONS

  * `--ackmate`:
    Output results in a format parseable by [AckMate](https://github.com/protocool/AckMate).

  * `--[no]affinity`:
    Set thread affinity (if platform supports it). Default is true.

  * `-a --all-types`:
    Search all files. This doesn't include hidden files, and doesn't respect any ignore files.

  * `-A --after [LINES]`:
    Print lines after match. If not provided, LINES defaults to 2.

  * `-B --before [LINES]`:
    Print lines before match. If not provided, LINES defaults to 2.

  * `--[no]break`:
    Print a newline between matches in different files. Enabled by default.

  * `-c --count`:
    Only print the number of matches in each file.
    Note: This is the number of matches, **not** the number of matching lines.
    Pipe output to `wc -l` if you want the number of matching lines.

  * `--[no]color`:
    Print color codes in results. Enabled by default.

  * `--color-line-number`:
    Color codes for line numbers. Default is 1;33.

  * `--color-match`:
    Color codes for result match numbers. Default is 30;43.

  * `--color-path`:
    Color codes for path names. Default is 1;32.

  * `--column`:
    Print column numbers in results.

  * `-C --context [LINES]`:
    Print lines before and after matches. Default is 2.

  * `-D --debug`:
    Output ridiculous amounts of debugging info. Not useful unless you're actually debugging.

  * `--depth NUM`:
    Search up to NUM directories deep, -1 for unlimited. Default is 25.

  * `--[no]filename`:
    Print file names. Enabled by default, except when searching a single file.

  * `-f --[no]follow`:
    Follow symlinks. Default is false.

  * `-F --fixed-strings`:
    Alias for --literal for compatibility with grep.

  * `--[no]group`:
    The default, `--group`, lumps multiple matches in the same file
    together, and presents them under a single occurrence of the
    filename. `--nogroup` refrains from this, and instead places the
    filename at the start of each match line.

  * `-g PATTERN`:
    Print filenames matching PATTERN.

  * `-G --file-search-regex PATTERN`:
    Only search files whose names match PATTERN.

  * `-H --[no]heading`:
    Print filenames above matching contents.

  * `--hidden`:
    Search hidden files. This option obeys ignored files.

  * `--ignore PATTERN`:
    Ignore files/directories whose names match this pattern. Literal
    file and directory names are also allowed.

  * `--ignore-dir NAME`:
    Alias for --ignore for compatibility with ack.

  * `-i --ignore-case`:
    Match case-insensitively.

  * `-l --files-with-matches`:
    Only print the names of files containing matches, not the matching
    lines. An empty query will print all files that would be searched.

  * `-L --files-without-matches`:
    Only print the names of files that don't contain matches.

  * `--list-file-types`:
    See `FILE TYPES` below.

  * `-m --max-count NUM`:
    Skip the rest of a file after NUM matches. Default is 0, which never skips.

  * `--[no]mmap`:
    Toggle use of memory-mapped I/O. Defaults to true on platforms where
    `mmap()` is faster than `read()`. (All but macOS.)

  * `--[no]multiline`:
    Match regexes across newlines. Enabled by default.

  * `-n --norecurse`:
    Don't recurse into directories.

  * `--[no]numbers`:
    Print line numbers. Default is to omit line numbers when searching streams.

  * `-o --only-matching`:
    Print only the matching part of the lines.

  * `--one-device`:
    When recursing directories, don't scan dirs that reside on other storage
    devices. This lets you avoid scanning slow network mounts.
    This feature is not supported on all platforms.

  * `-p --path-to-ignore STRING`:
    Provide a path to a specific .ignore file.

  * `--pager COMMAND`:
    Use a pager such as `less`. Use `--nopager` to override. This option
    is also ignored if output is piped to another program.

  * `--parallel`:
    Parse the input stream as a search term, not data to search. This is meant
    to be used with tools such as GNU parallel. For example:
    `echo "foo\nbar\nbaz" | parallel "ag {} ."` will run 3 instances of ag,
    searching the current directory for "foo", "bar", and "baz".

  * `--print-long-lines`:
    Print matches on very long lines (> 2k characters by default).

  * `--passthrough --passthru`:
    When searching a stream, print all lines even if they don't match.

  * `-Q --literal`:
    Do not parse PATTERN as a regular expression. Try to match it literally.

  * `-r --recurse`:
    Recurse into directories when searching. Default is true.

  * `-s --case-sensitive`:
    Match case-sensitively.

  * `-S --smart-case`:
    Match case-sensitively if there are any uppercase letters in PATTERN,
    case-insensitively otherwise. Enabled by default.

  * `--search-binary`:
    Search binary files for matches.

  * `--silent`:
    Suppress all log messages, including errors.

  * `--stats`:
    Print stats (files scanned, time taken, etc).

  * `--stats-only`:
    Print stats (files scanned, time taken, etc) and nothing else.

  * `-t --all-text`:
    Search all text files. This doesn't include hidden files.

  * `-u --unrestricted`:
    Search *all* files. This ignores .ignore, .gitignore, etc. It searches
    binary and hidden files as well.

  * `-U --skip-vcs-ignores`:
    Ignore VCS ignore files (.gitignore, .hgignore), but still
    use .ignore.

  * `-v --invert-match`:
    Match every line *not* containing the specified pattern.

  * `-V --version`:
    Print version info.

  * `--vimgrep`:
    Output results in the same form as Vim's `:vimgrep /pattern/g`

    Here is a ~/.vimrc configuration example:

    `set grepprg=ag\ --vimgrep\ $*`
    `set grepformat=%f:%l:%c:%m`

    Then use `:grep` to grep for something.
    Then use `:copen`, `:cn`, `:cp`, etc. to navigate through the matches.

  * `-w --word-regexp`:
    Only match whole words.

  * `--workers NUM`:
    Use NUM worker threads. Default is the number of CPU cores, with a max of 8.

  * `-W --width NUM`:
    Truncate match lines after NUM characters.

  * `-z --search-zip`:
    Search contents of compressed files. Currently, gz and xz are supported.
    This option requires that ag is built with lzma and zlib.

  * `-0 --null --print0`:
    Separate the filenames with `\0`, rather than `\n`:
    this allows `xargs -0 <command>` to correctly process filenames containing
    spaces or newlines.


## FILE TYPES

It is possible to restrict the types of files searched. For example, passing
`--html` will search only files with the extensions `htm`, `html`, `shtml`
or `xhtml`. For a list of supported types, run `ag --list-file-types`.

## IGNORING FILES

By default, ag will ignore files whose names match patterns in .gitignore,
.hgignore, or .ignore. These files can be anywhere in the directories being
searched. Binary files are ignored by default as well. Finally, ag looks in
$HOME/.agignore for ignore patterns.

If you want to ignore .gitignore and .hgignore, but still take .ignore into
account, use `-U`.

Use the `-t` option to search all text files; `-a` to search all files; and `-u`
to search all, including hidden files.

## EXAMPLES

`ag printf`:
  Find matches for "printf" in the current directory.

`ag foo /bar/`:
  Find matches for "foo" in path /bar/.

`ag -- --foo`:
  Find matches for "--foo" in the current directory. (As with most UNIX command
  line utilities, "--" is used to signify that the remaining arguments should
  not be treated as options.)

## ABOUT

ag was originally created by Geoff Greer. More information (and the latest
release) can be found at http://geoff.greer.fm/ag

## SEE ALSO

grep(1)
</output>

def is_binary(data):
    """Check if data appears to be binary."""
    if not data:
        return False
    # Check for null bytes (common in binary files)
    # Check first 8192 bytes
    sample = data[:8192]
    if b'\x00' in sample:
        return True
    return False

def parse_gitignore(path):
    """Parse a .gitignore/.ignore style file, returning list of patterns."""
    patterns = []
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', errors='replace') as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')
                if line and not line.startswith('#'):
                    patterns.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return patterns

def parse_hgignore(path):
    """Parse a .hgignore file, returning list of (type, pattern) tuples."""
    patterns = []
    syntax = 'regexp'
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', errors='replace') as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')
                if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                if line.startswith('syntax:'):
                    s = line[7:].strip()
                    if s in ('glob', 'regexp'):
                        syntax = s
                    continue
                patterns.append((syntax, line))
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return patterns

def gitignore_pattern_to_regex(pattern, base_dir):
    """Convert a gitignore pattern to a regex that matches paths."""
    original = pattern
    
    # Negation
    negated = pattern.startswith('!')
    if negated:
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    
    # Trailing spaces (unless escaped)
    pattern = pattern.rstrip()
    
    if not pattern:
        return None, negated
    
    # A pattern ending with / only matches directories
    dir_only = pattern.endswith('/')
    if dir_only:
        pattern = pattern[:-1]
    
    # If pattern contains /, match relative to base_dir
    # If no /, match anywhere in tree
    anchored = '/' in pattern
    
    # Build regex
    # Convert glob to regex
    regex_parts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(pattern):
        c = pattern[i]
        if c == '\\' and i + 1 < len(pattern):
            regex_parts.append(re.escape(pattern[i+1]))
            i += 2
        elif c == '*':
            if i + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[i+1] == '*':
                # ** matches anything including /
                if i + 2 < len(pattern) and pattern[i+2] == '/':
                    regex_parts.append('(?:.+/)?')
                    i += 3
                else:
                    regex_parts.append('.*')
                    i += 2
            else:
                # * matches anything except /
                regex_parts.append('[^/]*')
                i += 1
        elif c == '?':
            regex_parts.append('[^/]')
            i += 1
        elif c == '[':
            # character class
            j = i + 1
            if j < len(pattern) and pattern[j] == '!':
                j += 1
            if j < len(pattern) and pattern[j] == ']':
                j += 1
            while j < len(pattern) and pattern[j] != ']':
                j += 1
            char_class = pattern[i:j+1]
            if char_class.startswith('[!'):
                char_class = '[^' + char_class[2:]
            regex_parts.append(char_class)
            i = j + 1
        else:
            regex_parts.append(re.escape(c))
            i += 1
    
    regex_str = ''.join(regex_parts)
    
    if anchored:
        # Match relative to base_dir
        full_regex = '(?:^|/)' + regex_str + ('(?:/|$)' if dir_only else '(?:/.*)?$')
    else:
        # Match anywhere
        full_regex = '(?:^|/)' + regex_str + ('(?:/|$)' if dir_only else '(?:/.*)?$')
    
    try:
        return re.compile(full_regex), negated
    except re.error:
        return None, negated

class IgnoreRules:
    """Manages ignore rules from various sources."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.rules = []  # list of (regex, negated, dir_only, base_dir)
    
    def add_gitignore_file(self, filepath, base_dir):
        """Load patterns from a gitignore-style file."""
        patterns = parse_gitignore(filepath)
        for pattern in patterns:
            original = pattern
            negated = pattern.startswith('!')
            if negated:
                pattern = pattern[1:]
            pattern = pattern.rstrip()
            if not pattern:
                continue
            dir_only = pattern.endswith('/')
            if dir_only:
                pattern = pattern[:-1]
            
            compiled, neg = gitignore_pattern_to_regex(original, base_dir)
            if compiled:
                self.rules.append((compiled, negated, dir_only, base_dir))
    
    def add_pattern(self, pattern, base_dir='/'):
        """Add a single ignore pattern."""
        compiled, negated = gitignore_pattern_to_regex(pattern, base_dir)
        dir_only = pattern.rstrip().endswith('/')
        if compiled:
            self.rules.append((compiled, negated, dir_only, base_dir))
    
    def is_ignored(self, path, is_dir=False, base_dir=None):
        """Check if a path should be ignored."""
        ignored = False
        # Normalize path
        path = path.replace(os.sep, '/')
        
        for regex, negated, dir_only, rule_base in self.rules:
            if dir_only and not is_dir:
                continue
            # Try to match
            if regex.search(path):
                if negated:
                    ignored = False
                else:
                    ignored = True
        
        return ignored

def should_ignore_path(path, is_dir, ignore_rules_list, cmd_ignore_patterns):
    """Check if a path should be ignored given a list of IgnoreRules objects."""
    basename = os.path.basename(path)
    
    # Check command-line ignore patterns
    for pattern in cmd_ignore_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(basename, pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern):
            return True
    
    # Check ignore rules
    rel_path = path  # Use the full path for matching
    for ignore_rules in ignore_rules_list:
        if ignore_rules.is_ignored(rel_path, is_dir):
            return True
    
    return False

class Searcher:
    def __init__(self, opts):
        self.opts = opts
        self.total_matches = 0
        self.total_files_searched = 0
        self.total_bytes_searched = 0
        self.files_with_matches = 0
        self.first_file_output = True
        
    def compile_pattern(self, pattern):
        """Compile the search pattern into a regex."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if opts.literal:
            pattern = re.escape(pattern)
        
        if opts.word_regexp:
            pattern = r'\b' + pattern + r'\b'
        
        flags = re.MULTILINE
        
        # Smart case: if pattern has uppercase, use case sensitive
        if opts.ignore_case:
            flags |= re.IGNORECASE
        elif opts.case_sensitive:
            pass  # no IGNORECASE
        else:
            # Smart case: if any uppercase in literal pattern, case sensitive
            # Need to check the original (unescaped if literal) pattern
            orig = opts.pattern if opts.literal else pattern
            has_upper = any(c.isupper() for c in opts.pattern)
            if not has_upper:
                flags |= re.IGNORECASE
        
        if opts.multiline:
            flags |= re.DOTALL
        
        try:
            return re.compile(pattern, flags)
        except re.error as e:
            print(f"ERR: Bad regex: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    
    def format_match_line(self, linenum, line, matches, is_context=False, sep='-'):
        """Format a single matched line for output."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if is_context:
            # Context line
            if opts.numbers:
                prefix = f"{linenum}{sep}"
            else:
                prefix = ""
            return prefix + line
        
        # Match line
        if opts.only_matching:
            result = []
            for m in matches:
                match_text = m.group(0)
                if opts.color:
                    result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{match_text}\033[0m\033[K")
                else:
                    result.append(match_text)
            return '\n'.join(result)
        
        # Build line with highlighted matches
        result = []
        pos = 0
        for m in matches:
            start, end = m.start(), m.end()
            if opts.color:
                result.append(line[pos:start])
                result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{line[start:end]}\033[0m\033[K")
            else:
                result.append(line[pos:end])
            pos = end
        result.append(line[pos:])
        content = ''.join(result)
        
        # Apply width truncation
        if opts.width > 0:
            # Truncate content (raw, ignoring ANSI codes for length calculation)
            raw_len = len(line)
            if raw_len > opts.width:
                # Truncate the original and add [...]
                trunc_line = line[:opts.width]
                # Redo matches with truncated line
                result = []
                pos = 0
                for m in matches:
                    start, end = m.start(), m.end()
                    if end > opts.width:
                        end = opts.width
                    if start >= opts.width:
                        break
                    if opts.color:
                        result.append(trunc_line[pos:start])
                        result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{trunc_line[start:end]}\033[0m\033[K")
                    else:
                        result.append(trunc_line[pos:end])
                    pos = end
                result.append(trunc_line[pos:])
                content = ''.join(result) + " [...]"
        
        if opts.numbers:
            if opts.color:
                prefix = f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:"
            else:
                prefix = f"{linenum}:"
            if opts.column and matches:
                col = matches[0].start() + 1
                if opts.color:
                    prefix = f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{col}\033[0m\033[K:"
                else:
                    prefix = f"{linenum}:{col}:"
        else:
            prefix = ""
        
        return prefix + content
    
    def format_context_line(self, linenum, line):
        """Format a context (non-match) line."""
        opts = self.opts
        if opts.numbers:
            if opts.color:
                return f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K-{line}"
            else:
                return f"{linenum}-{line}"
        else:
            return line
    
    def search_file_content(self, filepath, content, filename_for_output):
        """Search file content and return (matches_list, output_lines)."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        # Split into lines
        # Handle both \r\n and \n
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            try:
                text = content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
            except:
                text = content.decode('latin-1', errors='replace')
        else:
            text = content
        
        if opts.multiline and not opts.only_matching:
            # For multiline matching, we need to find matches across lines
            return self._search_multiline(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
        else:
            return self._search_linewise(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
    
    def _search_multiline(self, filepath, text, filename_for_output):
        """Handle multiline searching."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        # Find all matches in the full text
        all_matches = list(regex.finditer(text))
        
        if not all_matches:
            return 0, []
        
        if opts.invert_match:
            return self._search_linewise(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
        
        # Build line index
        lines = text.split('\n')
        # Handle trailing newline
        if text.endswith('\n'):
            lines = lines[:-1]
        
        # Build offset to line number mapping
        line_offsets = []
        offset = 0
        for line in lines:
            line_offsets.append(offset)
            offset += len(line) + 1  # +1 for \n
        
        def offset_to_linenum(off):
            lo, hi = 0, len(line_offsets) - 1
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if line_offsets[mid] <= off:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            return lo + 1  # 1-indexed
        
        # Group matches by which lines they span
        match_lines = set()
        for m in all_matches:
            start_line = offset_to_linenum(m.start())
            end_offset = m.end() - 1 if m.end() > m.start() else m.end()
            end_line = offset_to_linenum(end_offset)
            for ln in range(start_line, end_line + 1):
                match_lines.add(ln)
        
        total_matches = len(all_matches)
        
        if opts.files_with_matches or opts.files_without_matches:
            return total_matches, []
        
        if opts.count:
            return total_matches, []
        
        # Build output lines
        output = self._build_output_from_matches(
            filepath, text, lines, line_offsets, all_matches, match_lines,
            filename_for_output
        )
        
        return total_matches, output
    
    def _build_output_from_matches(self, filepath, text, lines, line_offsets,
                                    all_matches, match_lines, filename_for_output):
        opts = self.opts
        
        # Map line numbers to their matches
        line_to_matches = {}
        for m in all_matches:
            # Find which line this match starts on
            lo, hi = 0, len(line_offsets) - 1
            start = m.start()
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if line_offsets[mid] <= start:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            ln = lo + 1
            if ln not in line_to_matches:
                line_to_matches[ln] = []
            line_to_matches[ln].append(m)
        
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        # Determine which lines to print
        lines_to_print = set()
        for ln in match_lines:
            for i in range(max(1, ln - before_ctx), min(len(lines), ln + after_ctx) + 1):
                lines_to_print.add(i)
        
        sorted_lines = sorted(lines_to_print)
        
        prev_printed = None
        for i, ln in enumerate(sorted_lines):
            if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                output.append('--')
            
            line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
            
            if ln in match_lines:
                matches_for_line = line_to_matches.get(ln, [])
                formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches_for_line)
                output.append(formatted)
            else:
                formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                output.append(formatted)
            
            prev_printed = ln
        
        return output
    
    def _search_linewise(self, filepath, text, filename_for_output):
        """Search line by line."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        lines = text.split('\n')
        if text.endswith('\n'):
            lines = lines[:-1]
        
        total_matches = 0
        match_line_nums = []
        line_matches = {}
        
        max_count = opts.max_count
        
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            linenum = i + 1
            
            if opts.invert_match:
                if not regex.search(line):
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = []
                    total_matches += 1
            else:
                matches = list(regex.finditer(line))
                if matches:
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = matches
                    total_matches += len(matches)
                    if max_count > 0 and total_matches >= max_count:
                        if total_matches > max_count:
                            print(f"ERR: Too many matches in {filepath}. Skipping the rest of this file.",
                                  file=sys.stderr)
                        break
        
        if not match_line_nums:
            return 0, []
        
        if opts.files_with_matches or opts.files_without_matches:
            return total_matches, []
        
        if opts.count:
            return total_matches, []
        
        # Build output
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        if before_ctx == 0 and after_ctx == 0:
            # Simple case - no context
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                line = lines[linenum - 1]
                matches = line_matches[linenum]
                if opts.only_matching:
                    for m in matches:
                        match_text = m.group(0)
                        if opts.color:
                            output.append(
                                (f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:" if opts.numbers else "") +
                                f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{match_text}\033[0m\033[K"
                            )
                        else:
                            output.append(
                                (f"{linenum}:" if opts.numbers else "") + match_text
                            )
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(linenum, line, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
        else:
            # Context mode
            lines_to_print = {}
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                for ctx_ln in range(max(1, linenum - before_ctx),
                                    min(len(lines), linenum + after_ctx) + 1):
                    if ctx_ln in lines_to_print:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = lines_to_print[ctx_ln] or (ctx_ln == linenum)
                    else:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = (ctx_ln == linenum)
            
            prev_printed = None
            for ln in sorted(lines_to_print.keys()):
                is_match = lines_to_print[ln]
                
                if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                    output.append('--')
                
                line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
                
                if is_match:
                    matches = line_matches.get(ln, [])
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                    output.append(formatted)
                
                prev_printed = ln
        
        return total_matches, output
    
    def output_results(self, filepath, match_count, output_lines, is_single_file=False):
        """Output the results for a file."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if opts.stats_only:
            return
        
        if opts.files_without_matches:
            if match_count == 0:
                if opts.print_null:
                    sys.stdout.write(filepath + '\0')
                else:
                    print(filepath)
            return
        
        if match_count == 0 and not opts.files_without_matches:
            return
        
        if opts.files_with_matches:
            if match_count > 0:
                if opts.print_null:
                    sys.stdout.write(filepath + '\0')
                else:
                    print(filepath)
            return
        
        if opts.count:
            if match_count > 0:
                if opts.print_filename:
                    if opts.color:
                        print(f"\033[{opts.color_path}m{filepath}\033[0m\033[K:{match_count}")
                    else:
                        print(f"{filepath}:{match_count}")
                else:
                    print(match_count)
            return
        
        if not output_lines:
            return
        
        # Determine if we should print filename header
        show_filename = opts.print_filename and not is_single_file
        # Single file: don't show filename unless --filename is explicitly set
        if opts.filename_explicit:
            show_filename = opts.print_filename
        
        if opts.heading and show_filename:
            # Print filename as header
            if not self.first_file_output and opts.do_break:
                print()
            if opts.color:
                print(f"\033[{opts.color_path}m{filepath}\033[0m\033[K")
            else:
                print(filepath)
            self.first_file_output = False
            for line in output_lines:
                print(line)
        elif not opts.heading and show_filename:
            # Prefix each line with filename
            if not self.first_file_output and opts.do_break:
                pass  # no break in noheading mode by default
            self.first_file_output = False
            
            # In ackmate mode
            if opts.ackmate:
                if not self.first_file_output_ackmate:
                    print()
                print(f":{filepath}")
                self.first_file_output_ackmate = False
                for line in output_lines:
                    print(line)
                return
            
            for line in output_lines:
                if opts.vimgrep:
                    # Already formatted by vimgrep handler
                    print(line)
                else:
                    # In noheading mode with filename, prefix file:line
                    # But output_lines already have the line format
                    if opts.color:
                        print(f"\033[{opts.color_path}m{filepath}\033[0m\033[K:{line}")
                    else:
                        print(f"{filepath}:{line}")
        else:
            # No filename shown (single file or --nofilename)
            self.first_file_output = False
            for line in output_lines:
                print(line)
    
    def search_file(self, filepath, is_single_file=False):
        """Search a single file."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                content = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError, PermissionError) as e:
            if not opts.silent:
                print(f"ERR: Skipping {filepath}: Error opening file: {e.strerror}",
                      file=sys.stderr)
            return
        
        self.total_files_searched += 1
        self.total_bytes_searched += len(content)
        
        # Check if binary
        if is_binary(content):
            if not opts.search_binary:
                return
            # For binary files, just report if it matches
            if isinstance(opts.compiled_pattern, type(re.compile(''))):
                try:
                    text = content.decode('latin-1')
                    if opts.compiled_pattern.search(text):
                        self.total_matches += 1
                        self.files_with_matches += 1
                        if not opts.stats_only:
                            print(f"Binary file {filepath} matches.")
                except:
                    pass
            return
        
        match_count, output_lines = self.search_file_content(filepath, content, filepath)
        
        if match_count > 0:
            self.total_matches += match_count
            self.files_with_matches += 1
        
        self.output_file_results(filepath, match_count, output_lines, is_single_file)
    
    def output_file_results(self, filepath, match_count, output_lines, is_single_file):
        """Output results for a file."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if opts.stats_only:
            return
        
        if opts.files_without_matches:

            filepath, text, lines, line_offsets, all_matches, match_lines,

        )

    def _build_output_from_matches(self, filepath, text, lines, line_offsets,

        line_to_matches = {}
        for m in all_matches:
            # Find which line this match starts on
            lo, hi = 0, len(line_offsets) - 1
            start = m.start()
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if line_offsets[mid] <= start:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            ln = lo + 1
            if ln not in line_to_matches:
                line_to_matches[ln] = []
            line_to_matches[ln].append(m)
        
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        # Determine which lines to print
        lines_to_print = set()
        for ln in match_lines:
            for i in range(max(1, ln - before_ctx), min(len(lines), ln + after_ctx) + 1):
                lines_to_print.add(i)
        
        sorted_lines = sorted(lines_to_print)
        
        prev_printed = None
        for i, ln in enumerate(sorted_lines):
            if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                output.append('--')
            
            line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
            
            if ln in match_lines:
                matches_for_line = line_to_matches.get(ln, [])
                formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches_for_line)
                output.append(formatted)
            else:
                formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                output.append(formatted)
            
            prev_printed = ln

    def _search_linewise(self, filepath, text, filename_for_output):
        """Search line by line."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        lines = text.split('\n')
        if text.endswith('\n'):
            lines = lines[:-1]
        
        total_matches = 0
        match_line_nums = []
        line_matches = {}
        
        max_count = opts.max_count
        
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            linenum = i + 1
            
            if opts.invert_match:
                if not regex.search(line):
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = []
                    total_matches += 1
            else:
                matches = list(regex.finditer(line))
                if matches:
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = matches
                    total_matches += len(matches)
                    if max_count > 0 and total_matches >= max_count:
                        if total_matches > max_count:
                            print(f"ERR: Too many matches in {filepath}. Skipping the rest of this file.",
                                  file=sys.stderr)
                        break
        
        if not match_line_nums:
            return 0, []
        
        if opts.files_with_matches or opts.files_without_matches:
            return total_matches, []
        
        if opts.count:
            return total_matches, []
        
        # Build output
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        if before_ctx == 0 and after_ctx == 0:
            # Simple case - no context
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                line = lines[linenum - 1]
                matches = line_matches[linenum]
                if opts.only_matching:
                    for m in matches:
                        match_text = m.group(0)
                        if opts.color:
                            output.append(

                                f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{match_text}\033[0m\033[K"
                            )
                        else:
                            output.append(
                                (f"{linenum}:" if opts.numbers else "") + match_text
                            )
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(linenum, line, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
        else:
            # Context mode
            lines_to_print = {}
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                for ctx_ln in range(max(1, linenum - before_ctx),
                                    min(len(lines), linenum + after_ctx) + 1):
                    if ctx_ln in lines_to_print:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = lines_to_print[ctx_ln] or (ctx_ln == linenum)
                    else:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = (ctx_ln == linenum)
            
            prev_printed = None
            for ln in sorted(lines_to_print.keys()):
                is_match = lines_to_print[ln]
                
                if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                    output.append('--')
                
                line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
                
                if is_match:
                    matches = line_matches.get(ln, [])
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                    output.append(formatted)
                
                prev_printed = ln
        
        return total_matches, output

class Searcher:
    def __init__(self, opts):

    def compile_pattern(self, pattern):
        """Compile the search pattern into a regex."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if opts.literal:
            pattern = re.escape(pattern)
        
        if opts.word_regexp:
            pattern = r'\b' + pattern + r'\b'
        
        flags = re.MULTILINE
        
        # Smart case: if pattern has uppercase, use case sensitive
        if opts.ignore_case:
            flags |= re.IGNORECASE
        elif opts.case_sensitive:
            pass  # no IGNORECASE
        else:
            # Smart case: if any uppercase in literal pattern, case sensitive
            # Need to check the original (unescaped if literal) pattern
            orig = opts.pattern if opts.literal else pattern
            has_upper = any(c.isupper() for c in opts.pattern)
            if not has_upper:
                flags |= re.IGNORECASE
        
        if opts.multiline:
            flags |= re.DOTALL
        
        try:
            return re.compile(pattern, flags)
        except re.error as e:
            print(f"ERR: Bad regex: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    
    def format_match_line(self, linenum, line, matches, is_context=False, sep='-'):
        """Format a single matched line for output."""
        opts = self.opts
        
        if is_context:

            if opts.numbers:
                prefix = f"{linenum}{sep}"
            else:
                prefix = ""

        # Match line

            result = []
            for m in matches:

                if opts.color:
                    result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{match_text}\033[0m\033[K")
                else:
                    result.append(match_text)
            return '\n'.join(result)

        result = []
        pos = 0
        for m in matches:
            start, end = m.start(), m.end()
            if opts.color:
                result.append(line[pos:start])
                result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{line[start:end]}\033[0m\033[K")
            else:
                result.append(line[pos:end])
            pos = end
        result.append(line[pos:])
        content = ''.join(result)
        
        # Apply width truncation
        if opts.width > 0:
            # Truncate content (raw, ignoring ANSI codes for length calculation)
            raw_len = len(line)
            if raw_len > opts.width:
                # Truncate the original and add [...]
                trunc_line = line[:opts.width]
                # Redo matches with truncated line
                result = []
                pos = 0
                for m in matches:
                    start, end = m.start(), m.end()
                    if end > opts.width:
                        end = opts.width
                    if start >= opts.width:
                        break
                    if opts.color:
                        result.append(trunc_line[pos:start])
                        result.append(f"\033[{opts.color_match}m{trunc_line[start:end]}\033[0m\033[K")
                    else:
                        result.append(trunc_line[pos:end])
                    pos = end
                result.append(trunc_line[pos:])
                content = ''.join(result) + " [...]"
        
        if opts.numbers:
            if opts.color:
                prefix = f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:"
            else:
                prefix = f"{linenum}:"
            if opts.column and matches:
                col = matches[0].start() + 1
                if opts.color:
                    prefix = f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{col}\033[0m\033[K:"
                else:
                    prefix = f"{linenum}:{col}:"
        else:
            prefix = ""
        
        return prefix + content
    
    def format_context_line(self, linenum, line):
        """Format a context (non-match) line."""
        opts = self.opts
        if opts.numbers:
            if opts.color:
                return f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K-{line}"
            else:
                return f"{linenum}-{line}"
        else:
            return line
    
    def search_file_content(self, filepath, content, filename_for_output):
        """Search file content and return (matches_list, output_lines)."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        # Split into lines
        # Handle both \r\n and \n
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            try:
                text = content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
            except:
                text = content.decode('latin-1', errors='replace')
        else:
            text = content
        
        if opts.multiline and not opts.only_matching:
            # For multiline matching, we need to find matches across lines
            return self._search_multiline(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
        else:
            return self._search_linewise(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
    
    def _search_multiline(self, filepath, text, filename_for_output):
        """Handle multiline searching."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        # Find all matches in the full text
        all_matches = list(regex.finditer(text))
        
        if not all_matches:
            return 0, []
        
        if opts.invert_match:
            return self._search_linewise(filepath, text, filename_for_output)
        
        # Build line index
        lines = text.split('\n')
        # Handle trailing newline
        if text.endswith('\n'):
            lines = lines[:-1]
        
        # Build offset to line number mapping
        line_offsets = []
        offset = 0
        for line in lines:
            line_offsets.append(offset)
            offset += len(line) + 1  # +1 for \n
        
        def offset_to_linenum(off):
            lo, hi = 0, len(line_offsets) - 1
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if line_offsets[mid] <= off:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            return lo + 1  # 1-indexed
        
        # Group matches by which lines they span
        match_lines = set()
        for m in all_matches:
            start_line = offset_to_linenum(m.start())
            end_offset = m.end() - 1 if m.end() > m.start() else m.end()
            end_line = offset_to_linenum(end_offset)
            for ln in range(start_line, end_line + 1):
                match_lines.add(ln)
        
        total_matches = len(all_matches)
        
        if opts.files_with_matches or opts.files_without_matches:
            return total_matches, []
        
        if opts.count:
            return total_matches, []
        
        # Build output lines
        output = self._build_output_from_matches(
            filepath, text, lines, line_offsets, all_matches, match_lines,
            filename_for_output
        )
        
        return total_matches, output
    
    def _build_output_from_matches(self, filepath, text, lines, line_offsets,
                                    all_matches, match_lines, filename_for_output):
        opts = self.opts
        
        # Map line numbers to their matches
        line_to_matches = {}
        for m in all_matches:
            # Find which line this match starts on
            lo, hi = 0, len(line_offsets) - 1
            start = m.start()
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if line_offsets[mid] <= start:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            ln = lo + 1
            if ln not in line_to_matches:
                line_to_matches[ln] = []
            line_to_matches[ln].append(m)
        
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        # Determine which lines to print
        lines_to_print = set()
        for ln in match_lines:
            for i in range(max(1, ln - before_ctx), min(len(lines), ln + after_ctx) + 1):
                lines_to_print.add(i)
        
        sorted_lines = sorted(lines_to_print)
        
        prev_printed = None
        for i, ln in enumerate(sorted_lines):
            if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                output.append('--')
            
            line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
            
            if ln in match_lines:
                matches_for_line = line_to_matches.get(ln, [])
                formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches_for_line)
                output.append(formatted)
            else:
                formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                output.append(formatted)
            
            prev_printed = ln
        
        return output
    
    def _search_linewise(self, filepath, text, filename_for_output):
        """Search line by line."""
        opts = self.opts
        regex = opts.compiled_pattern
        
        lines = text.split('\n')
        if text.endswith('\n'):
            lines = lines[:-1]
        
        total_matches = 0
        match_line_nums = []
        line_matches = {}
        
        max_count = opts.max_count
        
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            linenum = i + 1
            
            if opts.invert_match:
                if not regex.search(line):
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = []
                    total_matches += 1
            else:
                matches = list(regex.finditer(line))
                if matches:
                    match_line_nums.append(linenum)
                    line_matches[linenum] = matches
                    total_matches += len(matches)
                    if max_count > 0 and total_matches >= max_count:
                        if total_matches > max_count:
                            print(f"ERR: Too many matches in {filepath}. Skipping the rest of this file.",
                                  file=sys.stderr)
                        break
        
        if not match_line_nums:
            return 0, []
        
        if opts.files_with_matches or opts.files_without_matches:
            return total_matches, []
        
        if opts.count:
            return total_matches, []
        
        # Build output
        output = []
        before_ctx = opts.before_context
        after_ctx = opts.after_context
        
        if before_ctx == 0 and after_ctx == 0:
            # Simple case - no context
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                line = lines[linenum - 1]
                matches = line_matches[linenum]
                if opts.only_matching:
                    for m in matches:
                        match_text = m.group(0)
                        if opts.color:
                            output.append(
                                (f"\033[{opts.color_line_number}m{linenum}\033[0m\033[K:" if opts.numbers else "") +

                            )
                        else:
                            output.append(
                                (f"{linenum}:" if opts.numbers else "") + match_text
                            )
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(linenum, line, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
        else:
            # Context mode
            lines_to_print = {}
            for linenum in match_line_nums:
                for ctx_ln in range(max(1, linenum - before_ctx),
                                    min(len(lines), linenum + after_ctx) + 1):
                    if ctx_ln in lines_to_print:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = lines_to_print[ctx_ln] or (ctx_ln == linenum)
                    else:
                        lines_to_print[ctx_ln] = (ctx_ln == linenum)
            
            prev_printed = None
            for ln in sorted(lines_to_print.keys()):
                is_match = lines_to_print[ln]
                
                if prev_printed is not None and ln > prev_printed + 1:
                    output.append('--')
                
                line_content = lines[ln - 1] if ln <= len(lines) else ''
                
                if is_match:
                    matches = line_matches.get(ln, [])
                    formatted = self.format_match_line(ln, line_content, matches)
                    output.append(formatted)
                else:
                    formatted = self.format_context_line(ln, line_content)
                    output.append(formatted)
                
                prev_printed = ln
        
        return total_matches, output

def is_binary(data):
    """Check if data appears to be binary."""
    if not data:
        return False
    # Check for null bytes (common in binary files)
    # Check first 8192 bytes
    sample = data[:8192]
    if b'\x00' in sample:
        return True
    return False
